messages.subject: PyStan running old models
parts:
I've noticed that PyStan doesn't actually update the model if the code changes unless you restart the Python interpreter. I'm midway through debugging that, but wanted to give a heads-up: if you're having inexplicable problems with a model, try restarting.

A demonstration (I'm actually using ipython, though):

>>> import pystan
>>> m_y = pystan.StanModel(model_code='parameters {real y;} model {y ~ normal(0,1);}')
>>> m_y.optimizing()['par']['y']
array(0.0) # success.
>>> m_z = pystan.StanModel(model_code='parameters {real z;} model {z ~ normal(0,1);}')
>>> m_z.optimizing()['par']['z']
KeyError # because it's actually running m_y!
>>> m_z = pystan.StanModel(model_code='parameters {real z;} model {z ~ normal(0,1);}', model_name='m_z')
>>> m_z.optimizing()['par']['z']
array(0.0) # success.

I've also noticed that if you pickle the StanModel object and reload it in a new session, it correctly runs the new model.

The different models are indeed using new Python module names (there was a tiny bug in the case of loading model code from a a file that had previously made it re-use the same module name. The probably more common case of passing the code as a string gets that tricky detail correct. I'll submit a PR shortly):

>>> [k for k in sys.modules.keys() if 'stanfit' in k]
['stanfit4anon_model_08e08668c8f51816387d4a09ca3747a7',
 'stanfit4anon_model_1079b7dbebb119312268da41f2eee749',
 'stanfit4m_z_32c35ac5f3514fe587f3e01fda9796b0']

What I suspect is going on is that while the Python module is fine, the exported symbols from the C++ code itself are already in the process and so aren't reloaded. They're namespaced under the model name, which would explain why changing the model name makes it work. I'm a bit perplexed why the tests pass, though, since not all of them set model_name. I'm not certain I've run the full testsuite on my toolchain, though.

I'll probably make the interim patch of appending a hash of the model code to the C++ model name. But I suspect the issue could be avoided entirely if the model C++ functions didn't end up exported. And maybe it's just a quirk of my toolchain (clang++ 5, see below) that makes this happen at all. How does RStan handle this?

-Ken
